source.title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory

accepted.question_text: Can one construct rational two-dimensional conformal field theories satisfying the Kontsevich, Segal, and Moore-Seiberg axioms, or at least prove that such theories exist, including Wess-Zumino-Witten models and minimal models? A complete construction should include higher-genus correlation functions and a locally convex complete topological state space with a nondegenerate Hermitian form, rather than only genus-zero and genus-one data or a graded state space.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Construct rational conformal field theories satisfying the axioms of Kontsevich, G. Segal [Se] and Moore-Seiberg [MS1] [MS2], or at least prove the existence of such rational conformal field theories. In particular, construct the Wess-Zumino-Witten models and minimal models or at least prove their existence.

But there is still no construction of the higher-genus correlation functions. Also, the state space obtained in these constructions is only a graded space with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear or Hermitian form. To construct the conformal field theories completely, we also need to construct a locally convex complete topological vector space with a nondegenerate Hermitian form.

accepted.question_text: For higher-genus correlation functions of rational conformal field theories, can one prove convergence of the series built from intertwining operators, so that their sums define functions on Teichmuller spaces and yield higher-genus chiral and full correlation functions?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Prove the convergence of these series obtained using intertwining operators to construct higher-genus correlation functions.

accepted.question_text: If the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has a compatible inner product, meaning an inner product invariant under conformal fields constructed from intertwining operators, is the locally convex topological completion obtained by adding elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces isomorphic to its Hilbert space completion as a locally convex topological vector space with grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form?

evidence.quote: If the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has an inner product invariant under the conformal fields constructed from intertwining operators (we call it a compatible inner product), then this graded state space also has a Hilbert space completion.

Conjecture 2.3. If the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has a compatible inner product, then the locally convex topological completion obtained by adding elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces and the Hilbert space completion are isomorphic as locally convex topological vector spaces with grading structures and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian forms.

accepted.question_text: For a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, is every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length completely reducible exactly when, for every positive integer n, the nth cohomology of the algebra with coefficients in any bimodule is zero? In particular, does the same equivalence hold for a grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, allowing the left and right bimodule actions to differ?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. Every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length for a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra is completely reducible if and only if for n in Z+, the n-th cohomology of the meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any bimodule is 0. In particular, every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length for a grading-restricted vertex algebra is completely reducible if and only if for n in Z+, the n-th cohomology of the grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any bimodule (whose left and right actions can be different) is 0.

accepted.question_text: For a vertex operator algebra V associated to a Wess-Zumino-Witten model, a minimal model, a lattice vertex operator algebra, or the moonshine module vertex operator algebra, does the nth cohomology of V, viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any V-bimodule, vanish for every positive integer n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. Let V be a vertex operator algebra associated to a Wess-Zumino-Witten model, a minimal model, a lattice vertex operator algebra or the moonshine module vertex operator algebra. Then for n in Z+, the n-th cohomology of V as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any V-bimodule is 0.

accepted.question_text: Can one find a criterion stated in terms of a grading-restricted vertex algebra itself that determines complete reducibility of its modules?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3. Find a criterion on a grading-restricted vertex algebra itself for the complete reducibility of modules.

accepted.question_text: Can one study the moduli space of two-dimensional conformal field theories by defining topological and geometric structures on it, and prove that rational conformal field theories are isolated points in this moduli space?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Study the moduli space of conformal field theories. Give topological and geometric structures on the moduli space. Prove that rational conformal field theories are isolated points in the moduli space.

accepted.question_text: For grading-restricted vertex algebras, what conditions make formal deformations converge to analytic deformations, and can the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras be generalized to genus-zero full conformal field theories?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Find the conditions for the formal deformations of grading-restricted vertex algebras to converge to analytic deformations. Generalize the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras to a deformation theory of genus-zero full conformal field theories.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a simple vertex operator algebra such that V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, the contragredient V-module V' is equivalent to V, and V is C2-cofinite, meaning dim V/C2(V)<infinity where C2(V) is spanned by Res_x x^-2 Y(u,x)v for u,v in V and Y is the vertex operator map. Is the braided tensor category of grading-restricted generalized V-modules constructed from logarithmic tensor-category theory rigid?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Assume that V is a simple vertex operator algebra satisfying the following conditions: (1) V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n < 0 and the contragredient V', as a V-module, is equivalent to V.

(2) V is C2-cofinite, that is, dim V/C2(V) < infinity, where C2(V) is the subspace of V spanned by the elements of the form Res_x x^-2Y(u,x)v for u, v in V and Y : V tensor V -> V[[x, x^-1]] is the vertex operator map for V. Then the braided tensor category given in [H8] based on the work [HLZ1]-[HLZ9] is rigid.

accepted.question_text: In the nonsemisimple setting relevant to logarithmic conformal field theories, can one define the correct notion of modular tensor category and prove that the braided tensor category of grading-restricted generalized modules for a simple C2-cofinite vertex operator algebra satisfying V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, and V' equivalent to V has this structure? From such a nonsemisimple modular tensor category, can one still construct a three-dimensional topological quantum field theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds?

evidence.quote: For a logarithmic conformal field theory, since the category is not semisimple, it is not sufficient to consider only irreducible modules. So giving the correct definition of modular tensor category in the case of logarithmic conformal field theories is also an important unsolved problem.

Problem 5.2. Give a definition of modular tensor category in the nonsemisimple case and prove that the braided tensor category in Conjecture 5.1 has such a modular tensor category structure. From such a nonsemisimple modular tensor category, can we still construct a 3-dimensional topological quantum field theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds?

accepted.question_text: For a simple vertex operator algebra V satisfying V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, V' equivalent to V, and C2-cofiniteness, can genus-zero and genus-one full logarithmic conformal-field-theory correlation functions be constructed from the corresponding chiral correlation functions? Can those correlation functions produce a conformal field theory satisfying the Kontsevich-Segal axioms except for unitarity?

evidence.quote: The associativity of logarithmic intertwining operators and the modular invariance of logarithmic intertwining operators discussed above gave the genus-zero and genus-one chiral correlation functions in the corresponding logarithmic conformal field theory. But we do not know how to construct the genus-zero and genus-one full correlation functions for the logarithmic full conformal field theory.

Problem 5.3. For a vertex operator algebra satisfying the conditions in Conjecture 5.1, is it possible to construct genus-zero and genus-one full correlation functions from the genus-zero and genus-one chiral correlation functions? From these genus-zero and genus-one correlation functions, is it possible to construct a conformal field theory satisfying the axioms of Kontsevich-Segal, except for the axioms involving unitarity?

accepted.question_text: Let V be a simple C2-cofinite vertex operator algebra with V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, V' equivalent to V, and every grading-restricted generalized V-module completely reducible, and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V. Do the twisted intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules, for all g in G, satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.1. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the two conditions in Conjecture 5.1. Assume that in addition every grading-restricted generalized V-module is completely reducible. Let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V. Then the twisted intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a simple C2-cofinite vertex operator algebra with V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, V' equivalent to V, and every grading-restricted generalized V-module completely reducible, and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V. Is the category of g-twisted V-modules for all g in G a G-crossed tensor category in Turaev's sense?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.2. Let V be a vertex operator satisfying the three conditions in Conjecture 6.1 and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V. The category of g-twisted V-modules for all g in G is a G-crossed (tensor) category in the sense of Turaev [T2].

accepted.question_text: Let V be a simple C2-cofinite vertex operator algebra with V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, V' equivalent to V, and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V, without assuming complete reducibility. Do the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among all g-twisted V-modules satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.3. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the two conditions in Conjecture 5.1 and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V. Then the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties.

accepted.question_text: For a vertex operator algebra V and an infinite group G of automorphisms of V, under what conditions do twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance? Under what conditions is the category of all such g-twisted V-modules a G-crossed tensor category?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4. Let V be a vertex operator algebra and let G be a group of automorphisms of V. If G is an infinite group, under what conditions do the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties? Under what conditions is the category of g-twisted V-modules for all g in G a G-crossed (tensor) category?

accepted.question_text: Is every vertex operator algebra V with central charge 24, no nonzero weight-one elements, and the property that every irreducible V-module is equivalent to V while every V-module is completely reducible, necessarily isomorphic to the moonshine module vertex operator algebra?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the following three conditions: (1) The central charge of V is 24. (2) V has no nonzero elements of weight 1. (3) Any irreducible V module is equivalent to V as a V-module and every V-module is completely reducible. Then V must be isomorphic to the moonshine module vertex operator algebra.

accepted.question_text: For a vertex operator algebra V of central charge 24 such that every irreducible V-module is equivalent to V and every V-module is completely reducible, is V determined uniquely by the Lie algebra structure on its homogeneous subspace of weight one?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the following three conditions: (1) The central charge of V is 24.

Conjecture 7.2. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the first and the third conditions in Conjecture 7.1. Then V is determined uniquely by the Lie algebra structure on its homogeneous subspace of weight 1.

accepted.question_text: Can one construct a functor from the category of Calabi-Yau manifolds to the category of N=2 vertex operator superalgebras such that the Fermat quintic threefold maps to the N=2 vertex operator superalgebra for the Gepner model and deformations of Calabi-Yau manifolds correspond to deformations of N=2 superconformal field theories?

evidence.quote: To study these conjectures using the representation theory of vertex operator algebras, the first step is to construct the corresponding N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras, that is, vertex operator algebras with N = 2 superconformal structures.

Problem 8.1. Construct a functor from the category of Calabi-Yau manifolds to the category of N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras such that the Fermat quintic threefold corresponds to the N = 2 vertex operator superalgebra for the Gepner model and such that deformations of Calabi-Yau manifolds correspond to deformations of N = 2 superconformal field theories.

accepted.question_text: If N=2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manifolds can be constructed, can one develop their representation theory and use it to construct the corresponding N=2 superconformal field theories, including operator product expansion for intertwining operators, modular invariance, modular tensor categories in a suitable sense, and full N=2 superconformal field theories?
accepted.context_brief: Representation theory for Calabi-Yau N=2 VOAs

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2. If N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manifolds can be constructed, study the representation theory of these N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras. Use this representation theory to construct the corresponding N = 2 superconformal field theories, including the proof of the operator product expansion of intertwining operators, the proof of modular invariance, the construction of modular tensor categories (in a suitable sense), and the construction of full N = 2 superconformal field theories.

accepted.question_text: Assuming N=2 vertex operator superalgebras for Calabi-Yau manifolds, their basic representation theory, and full N=2 superconformal field theories can be constructed, can physicists' conjectures about Calabi-Yau manifolds, such as quantum cohomology and mirror symmetry, be formulated and proved mathematically using those structures?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.3. Suppose that N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manifolds can be constructed, that the basic results in the representation theory of these algebras can be obtained and that the full N = 2 superconformal field theories can be constructed. Formulate and prove the conjectures (for example, quantum cohomology and mirror symmetry) by physicists on Calabi-Yau manifolds by turning physicists' intuition into mathematical methods using these results and constructions.

accepted.question_text: Can one find a direct connection between the representation-theoretic vertex-operator-algebra approach to conformal field theory and the conformal-net approach, and prove that the two approaches are equivalent at least for rational conformal field theories?

evidence.quote: There are many different methods for the study of conformal field theories. But they can all be classified as belonging to one of two types of methods. The first type is the method of the representation theory of vertex operator algebras. The other is the method of conformal nets.

Problem 9.1. Find a direct connection between the method of the representation theory of vertex operator algebras and the method of conformal nets. Prove that at least for rational conformal field theories, they are equivalent.
